blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre filosofia da ciência a partir de uma entrevista, usando condicionais formais sobre falseabilidade e marcando a ênfase.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.intro: A historian of science discusses what separates science from pseudoscience.
qa: Interviewer: What did Karl Popper propose?
That a theory is scientific **only if** it **can in principle be refuted**. **Were** a theory compatible with every possible observation, it **would explain nothing**.
Interviewer: Is that still the standard?

**Not quite.** Philosophers **have since pointed out** that scientists rarely abandon a theory **at the first anomaly**. **Had** they done so, much of physics **would have been discarded** early. The picture is **messier** than a single rule.
Interviewer: So what is left of falsifiability?
**What remains** is the **attitude**: **seek the test** that could embarrass your hypothesis. **If** it survives, **then** your confidence is earned.

items.q: Popper said a theory is scientific only if it can be refuted.
The historian thinks falsifiability alone settles everything.
The interview names a specific experiment.

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
Sentido
rows: **Had** they done so, much **would have been discarded**
scientific **only if** it can be refuted

blocks.body: **Only if** marca condição **necessária**; **if** simples só dá condição suficiente. A inversão (*Were / Had*) é formal e substitui o *if*. Em fala, a ênfase cai em *only* e em *refuted*.
Não confunda *only if* (condição necessária) com *if and only if* (equivalência lógica).

items.s: A theory is scientific only ___ it can be refuted. (if)
___ a theory compatible with everything, it would explain nothing. (be, inversão)
___ they done so, physics would have been discarded. (have)
If it survives, ___ confidence is earned. (then)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Put to the test.** — Pôr à prova.
**Stand up to scrutiny.** — Resistir ao escrutínio.
**Back to the drawing board.** — Voltar à prancheta.
**Fly in the face of.** — Contrariar frontalmente.
**Hold water.** — Ser convincente.
**Clutch at straws.** — Agarrar-se a qualquer coisa.
**Fit the bill.** — Servir.
**Trial and error.** — Tentativa e erro.
**Beyond the pale.** — Inaceitável.
**Rule out.** — Descartar.
**And in practice?** — E na prática?
**So is a theory scientific only if it can be refuted?** — Então uma teoria é científica só se puder ser refutada?
**In principle, yes. Were it compatible with everything, it would explain nothing.** — Em princípio, sim. Se fosse compatível com tudo, nada explicaria.

prompts.model: A claim is testable only if it could fail.
Were the data to contradict it, I would revise my view.
Had they tested it, they would have noticed.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence explanation of why a testable claim is better than an untestable one, using only if, Were… and Had….
blocks.model: A claim is useful only if it could turn out false. Were a horoscope compatible with every outcome, it would predict nothing. Had its author named a risky prediction, we could have tested it. If the prediction fails, then we learn something. Scientists welcome such tests. That is what separates inquiry from comfort.

Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
